input_signals.name: AssetLightKnowledgeDeployment
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with large accumulated R&D investment and limited physical capital expansion should earn higher future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: High cumulative R&D scaled by assets captures a stock of knowledge capital, while low PP&E growth indicates asset-light deployment rather than heavy tangible expansion. The interaction targets firms where intangible capital may scale without requiring costly physical investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( xrd, 5 ), at ) ), rank( neg( growth( ppent, 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: DebtGoodwillGrossProfitGap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(dltt, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms increasing debt while goodwill rises faster than gross profit should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the sparse stock-financed-acquirer triple interaction and instead tests whether balance-sheet financing is backing acquired intangibles that are not yet producing gross-profit capacity. The signed spread compares purchased intangible accumulation with realized operating output, so the signal is not just an acquisition or issuance anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( dltt, at ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExternalFinancePhysicalTilt
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(sstk, at), DELTA(RATIO(dltt, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Externally financed shifts toward physical capex rather than R&D should predict lower returns when gross-profit productivity is not improving.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal directly compares the changing physical share of investment with realized gross-profit improvement, while conditioning on external funding pressure. This repairs the physical-share idea by asking whether financed tangible expansion is economically validated, rather than treating capex growth alone as the anomaly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sumrank( ratio( sstk, at ), delta( ratio( dltt, at ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( capx, add( capx, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashBurnPhysicalRDCrowding
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1))), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms drawing down cash while increasing capex intensity more than R&D intensity should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the duplicated goodwill-minus-gross-profit spread and instead tests whether internal liquidity is being consumed by tangible expansion rather than knowledge investment. The signed capex-versus-R&D change term distinguishes potentially productive cash-funded innovation from cash burn tied to physical overinvestment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PhysicalTiltGrossProfitMiss
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, ADD(capx, COALESCE(xrd, 0))), 1)), RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms shifting their investment mix toward physical capex and away from R&D while gross-profit productivity deteriorates should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the physical-share idea by conditioning the tangible shift on a direct operating payoff failure rather than sales growth alone. A high score identifies firms consuming investment capacity in physical assets without evidence that the broader intangible franchise is improving.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( capx, add( capx, coalesce( xrd, 0 ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: AcquisitionRevenueMarginDilution
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(aqc, 0), at)), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(sale, 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Acquisition-heavy firms that generate revenue growth without improving gross margins should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The revised sign treats goodwill- and acquisition-driven sales growth as suspect unless it improves the firm’s intangible pricing-power or cost advantage. This avoids rewarding recent asset-light acquirers merely because sales rise mechanically after consolidation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( aqc, 0 ), at ) ), sub( rank( growth( sale, 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: MoatFragileCapexLumpiness
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(VOL(RATIO(capx, at), 5)), SUB(RANK(VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Volatile capex should predict lower returns when the firm also has an unstable gross-margin franchise and weak R&D intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This converts the prior unconditioned low-volatility composite into a true interaction: capex lumpiness is penalized mainly when intangible franchise quality is fragile. Strong R&D intensity offsets the margin-instability leg, distinguishing innovation-backed experimentation from erratic physical investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( vol( ratio( capx, at ), 5 ) ), sub( rank( vol( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 5 ) ), rank( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: KnowledgeOptionAbandonment
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), at)), SUB(RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(capx, at), 1)), RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Historically R&D-intensive firms that pivot toward capex while R&D intensity weakens should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: A high prior R&D stock represents embedded growth options, but a subsequent shift toward physical investment may signal maturation or abandonment of the innovation pipeline. The signal is most negative when tangible investment rises relative to current R&D commitment, rather than simply rewarding or penalizing R&D intensity alone.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 5 ), at ) ), sub( rank( growth( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GrossProfitYieldOnKnowledgePPE
input_signals.expression: SUB(RANK(DELTA(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), ADD(ppent, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3))), 1), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms improving gross-profit yield on combined physical and R&D capital while avoiding goodwill accumulation should earn higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The numerator captures realized operating payoff, while the denominator combines tangible capital with accumulated R&D investment as productive capital inputs. Subtracting goodwill growth penalizes firms whose apparent capital formation comes from purchased intangibles rather than internally productive physical-plus-knowledge assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: sub( rank( delta( winsor( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), add( ppent, ts_sum( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), 3 ) ) ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityBuildDemandOptionGap
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppegt, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(sale, at), 5))), RANK(TREND(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms expanding gross physical capacity while sales productivity trends down and R&D intensity is not improving should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the prior splice with a capacity-timing mechanism: gross PPE buildup is most suspect when demand per asset is deteriorating. A rising R&D-intensity trend offsets the penalty, recognizing that temporary weak sales productivity may be acceptable if the firm is building physical capacity to commercialize knowledge assets.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( ppegt, at ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( neg( trend( ratio( sale, at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( trend( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GoodwillInventoryIntegrationRisk
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms adding goodwill while inventory intensity rises faster than gross margins improve should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the duplicated gross-profit-yield-on-PP&E-plus-goodwill term and instead tests whether purchased intangibles are creating integration or sell-through problems. Goodwill growth is most concerning when inventories accumulate without evidence of improving margin power, consistent with overpaid acquisitions or acquired products failing to convert into profitable demand.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), at ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( invt, sale ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: PPEIntensityCostPressureNoRD
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppent, sale), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, sale), 1)), RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms becoming more physical-capital intensive relative to sales while cost pressure rises and R&D intensity fails to improve should earn lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the duplicated gross-capacity gate with a direct deterioration in PP&E intensity per unit of revenue. The balanced rank spread compares rising cost burden against R&D improvement, avoiding the arbitrary SUMRANK-minus-single-rank offset.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( ppent, sale ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( cogs, sale ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CapacityInventoryNoInnovation
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppegt, at), 1)), SUB(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(invt, sale), 1)), RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Gross physical capacity expansion should predict lower returns when inventories build faster than R&D intensity improves.
input_signals.reasoning: Expanding gross PPE is most problematic when it is accompanied by poor sell-through rather than renewed innovation effort. The balanced spread distinguishes capacity additions tied to inventory accumulation from capacity additions supported by rising knowledge investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( ppegt, at ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( ratio( invt, sale ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProcessRDCapexCostRelief
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, ppent), 1)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, sale), 1))), RANK(NEG(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capex refresh should predict higher returns when it is associated with falling cost intensity and no cutback in R&D intensity.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the physical-share-versus-profit-erosion clone and instead tests whether tangible refresh is part of process innovation. The signal rewards capex only when costs improve and R&D is maintained or rising, distinguishing productive modernization from simple physical expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( capx, ppent ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( neg( delta( ratio( cogs, sale ), 1 ) ) ), rank( neg( delta( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: GoodwillCapexSupportBurden
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(ppent, COALESCE(gdwl, 0)))), SUB(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, ppent), 5)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Goodwill-heavy firms requiring unusually high capex support without margin improvement should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the goodwill-drawdown gate and instead uses goodwill concentration as an acquired-intangible overhang measure. High capex intensity is penalized only when it appears necessary to support goodwill-heavy assets without improving margins.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( coalesce( gdwl, 0 ), add( ppent, coalesce( gdwl, 0 ) ) ) ), sub( rank( ts_rank( ratio( capx, ppent ), 5 ) ), rank( delta( ratio( sub( sale, cogs ), sale ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: RDInvestmentCostEfficiency
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), 1)), SUB(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(cogs, sale), 1))), RANK(GROWTH(RATIO(capx, at), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Rising R&D intensity should predict higher returns when it coincides with cost-ratio improvement rather than heavy capex growth.
input_signals.reasoning: Productive intangible investment can improve process efficiency, product mix, or pricing relative to costs. The signal rewards R&D increases only when cost intensity falls and the improvement is not merely the result of expanding physical investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ma( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), sale ), 3 ), 1 ) ), sub( rank( neg( delta( ratio( cogs, sale ), 1 ) ) ), rank( growth( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: HiringTangiblePerWorkerTilt
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms hiring while increasing capex per employee more than R&D per employee should earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the prior operating-leverage construction and instead examines whether organizational expansion is equipped with tangible capital or knowledge capital. Hiring is penalized when the incremental investment per worker tilts toward physical assets rather than innovation.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( emp, 1 ) ), sub( rank( delta( winsor( ratio( capx, emp ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( delta( winsor( ratio( coalesce( xrd, 0 ), emp ), 1 ), 1 ) ) ) )
